title: arXiv Trending AI — Friday, 20 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from early independent technical discussion and corroborating signals, not readership statistics. Citation evidence is exceptionally limited for a batch announced less than two days ago.

sections.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
sections.abstract: The paper reports that fixed activation-steering vectors on frozen diffusion transformers reproduce most of the reward gains of several RL-post-trained image and video models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim that input-independent steering vectors recover 90.0–96.3% of reward gains across six RL-tuned image models and comparable gains on two video models, with far fewer parameters than an SD3.5-M LoRA.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated models use policy-gradient RL; preference optimization and reward backpropagation are explicitly left untested, and generality beyond the evaluated checkpoints remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Early discussion appears on Hugging Face Papers, an AI Crunch technical write-up, and a video analysis; it is cross-listed in vision and machine learning. Semantic Scholar showed 0 citations at lookup, so placement reflects corroborated discussion rather than citation momentum.

sections.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
sections.abstract: The paper introduces a stochastic diffusion-distillation objective that matches teacher posterior means to preserve conditional output diversity while supporting variable sampling steps.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors prove that matching exponentially tilted posterior means over an open neighborhood identifies the teacher posterior at zero population loss, and report best FID among four-step methods on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper states that training requires multiple student draws and still uses an auxiliary adversarial loss for visual realism; its posterior-identification result assumes an exact posterior-mean denoiser.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Early coverage appears on Papers with Code, ModelScope, and OpenTrain, plus a project page; these are technical discovery channels, not readership statistics. Citation totals were not available in the sources checked.

sections.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
sections.abstract: TideCache coordinates heterogeneous state and attention caches on CPU–GPU superchips, streaming attention-layer prefixes to reduce GPU residency while overlapping transfers with computation.
sections.claimed_contribution: In SGLang tests across seven configurations on GB300 and GH200, the authors report up to 2.04× as many agent turns, 20–59% lower overall P50 per-token latency, and 1.40–3.05× better agent P50 time-to-first-token than SGLang with HiCache.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is limited to two superchip platforms and the tested SGLang/model configurations; portability to ordinary accelerators or other serving stacks is not established here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Early technical commentary appeared at AI Crunch and Zhichai; the paper is cross-listed in machine learning despite its primary distributed-computing category. Semantic Scholar showed 0 citations at lookup; placement relies on the reported systems results and independent discussion.

sections.title: Pro$^2$ Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&D
sections.abstract: Pro$^2$ Agent makes an evolving, evidence-backed representation of bottlenecks and candidate solutions the state that guides an autonomous AI research agent’s experiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report matching the best published medal rate on complete MLE-Bench under 24 hours (70.7%) and reaching 76.0% with 48 hours, alongside competitive results on PostTrainBench.
sections.unique_caveat: The complete MLE-Bench comparison uses one run per budget; an independent AGI Hunt analysis also notes that published baselines differ in their underlying models, limiting causal attribution to the agent design.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper has a detailed independent analysis at AGI Hunt and a CatalyzeX listing, and spans AI and language. Semantic Scholar showed 0 citations at lookup; placement is based on early technical scrutiny and the benchmark claim, not citations.

sections.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
sections.abstract: Depth Pro 2 uses one scalable model to predict native-resolution metric depth for images and video, aiming to combine sharp boundaries with temporal consistency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a new Pareto frontier across metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime, and release a model family, code, and weights.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports aggregate superiority but does not specify the datasets, metric margins, or operating conditions; those details need checking before treating the claimed frontier as broadly established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work is accompanied by an Apple Machine Learning Research release and an OpenReview listing, with code and weights announced; it is cross-listed in machine learning. Semantic Scholar showed 0 citations at lookup, so the signal is release/discussion visibility rather than citation momentum.

sections.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
sections.abstract: AgentRoboCritic evaluates robot actions against each agent’s stated local intent, exposing action-level successes and failure modes across 12 manipulation benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors analyze direct control on 12 benchmarks and report a 12,844-action dataset, a 400-action human-annotated critic test set, and improved failure-mode accuracy after fine-tuning an open critic.
sections.unique_caveat: The intent-grounded critic depends on policy-generated local intent, and the paper’s human-annotated validation set contains 400 actions; independent validation with externally specified intents and more physical trials would test robustness.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A public project/repository and a DEV Community technical response provide early corroboration; the paper spans robotics, language, and vision. Citation totals were not available in the sources checked.

sections.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
sections.abstract: O$^{2}$LaF initializes inverse and forward dynamics from a shared video model to infer latent actions from unlabeled video and test their transfer across scenes and embodiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved few-shot action probing and zero-shot transfer in navigation and robot manipulation, including transfer from human demonstrations to robot demonstrations.
sections.unique_caveat: The robot-transfer evidence is based on the reported datasets and video evaluations; physical closed-loop deployment and broader embodiment coverage remain to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work has a project site and a Papers with Code entry, and unusually broad cross-listing across four core AI categories. Citation totals were not available in the sources checked; this is a relevance-led placement with limited attention evidence.

sections.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
sections.abstract: PlayCraft alternates between a vision-based player agent and a game-crafting agent that revises game rules and challenges using observed play and predicted learning progression.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes than initial games in most tested games, with better macro-average metrics than baselines across three player-agent intelligence settings.
sections.unique_caveat: Engagement and mastery are assessed through player agents and their learning metrics; human-player studies are needed to establish whether the generated games are enjoyable or teachable for people.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper has a public GitHub implementation and an AI Hot write-up; it is cross-listed in AI and vision. Semantic Scholar showed 0 citations at lookup; placement reflects early project-level discussion, not readership evidence.
